ahmedabad.title: Ahmedabad | Places To Visit in Gujarat | 99 Destinations
ahmedabad.content:
Ahmedabad | Places To Visit in Gujarat | 99 Destinations
Ahmedabad
Overview Ahmedabad
Ahmedabad – A City Where Heritage Meets Modern Gujarat
Ahmedabad, the largest city in Gujarat, is a fascinating blend of centuries-old heritage, vibrant culture, architectural treasures, and modern urban life. Founded by Sultan Ahmed Shah in the 15th century, the city has evolved into an important cultural, commercial, and educational centre while preserving the distinctive character of its historic neighbourhoods.
The city's heritage is best experienced through its old walled-city areas, traditional pol houses, intricately carved wooden architecture, historic mosques, temples, and bustling markets. The iconic **Sidi Saiyyed Mosque**, famous for its beautifully carved stone jali, and the historic **Jama Masjid** are among the architectural highlights that reflect Ahmedabad's rich Indo-Islamic heritage.
Ahmedabad also holds a special place in India's freedom movement. **Sabarmati Ashram**, situated beside the Sabarmati River, is closely associated with Mahatma Gandhi and remains one of the city's most significant heritage attractions. Visitors can explore the ashram's peaceful surroundings and learn about Gandhi's life, philosophy, and contribution to India's independence movement.
For a more contemporary experience, the **Sabarmati Riverfront** offers landscaped promenades, gardens, recreational spaces, and beautiful views along the river. **Kankaria Lake** is another popular destination, particularly for families, with recreational and entertainment attractions surrounding the lake.
The city is also home to several museums, cultural spaces, temples, and unique attractions such as **Amdavad Ni Gufa**, **Hutheesing Jain Temple**, **Sarkhej Roza**, and **Science City**. Together, these attractions showcase the diverse artistic, religious, scientific, and architectural identity of Ahmedabad.
No visit to Ahmedabad is complete without experiencing its local food and lively markets. From traditional Gujarati cuisine and street food to colourful textiles and handicrafts, the city offers visitors an opportunity to experience the flavours and everyday culture of Gujarat.
Whether you are interested in history, architecture, spirituality, culture, shopping, food, or family entertainment, Ahmedabad offers a diverse travel experience. Its combination of historic charm and modern attractions makes it an ideal destination for discovering the many layers of Gujarat.
Adalaj Stepwell
Located about 18 km from Ahmedabad near the village of Adalaj, the historic Adalaj Stepwell (Adalaj ni Vav) is one of Gujarat?s most remarkable architectural and cultural landmarks. Built in 1499 by Queen Rudabai, this five-storey stepwell served as both a water reservoir and a resting place for travelers along ancient trade routes. The structure is renowned for its exquisite Indo-Islamic architecture, beautifully carved pillars, ornate galleries, and intricate stone motifs depicting flowers, mythological scenes, and daily life. Designed to keep the interior cool even during peak summer, the stepwell demonstrates the brilliance of traditional water management systems in Gujarat. Sunlight filtering through the carved openings creates a mesmerizing play of light and shadow, making the monument a favorite among photographers and heritage enthusiasts. Today, Adalaj Stepwell stands as an important historical attraction near Ahmedabad, drawing tourists, historians, and architecture lovers who wish to explore Gujarat?s rich heritage and craftsmanship.
Auto World Vintage Car Museum
Discover the timeless charm of vintage automobiles at the Auto World Vintage Car Museum in Ahmedabad, one of the finest vintage car collections in India. Located in the serene Kathwada area, this fascinating museum showcases over a hundred rare classic vehicles including Rolls-Royce, Bentley, Cadillac, and Mercedes. Established by the passionate automobile enthusiast Pranlal Bhogilal, the museum reflects India?s royal motoring heritage and craftsmanship. Visitors can explore beautifully restored cars once owned by maharajas and global dignitaries. The museum also offers a unique opportunity to experience short vintage car rides, making it an unforgettable attraction for tourists and automobile lovers visiting Gujarat seeking history.
Calico Museum of Textiles
Located in the heart of Ahmedabad, the Calico Museum of Textiles is one of India?s most prestigious museums dedicated to the country?s rich textile heritage. Established in 1949 by the Sarabhai family, the museum showcases an extraordinary collection of rare fabrics, royal garments, intricate embroidery, and traditional weaving techniques dating from the 15th century onward. Visitors can admire exquisite Mughal court textiles, delicate Kashmiri shawls, vibrant Gujarati embroideries, temple cloths, and historic costumes that highlight India?s artistic and cultural legacy. Housed within the beautiful Sarabhai Haveli complex and surrounded by peaceful gardens, the museum offers a unique glimpse into centuries of craftsmanship and design excellence. Guided tours provide deep insight into the evolution of Indian textiles, natural dyeing processes, and regional weaving traditions. A visit to the Calico Museum of Textiles is a must for history lovers, art enthusiasts, and cultural travelers exploring Ahmedabad, making it one of the most significant heritage attractions in Gujarat tourism.
Dinosaur Fossil Park and Museum, Balasinor
Explore the prehistoric wonders of Dinosaur Fossil Park and Museum, Balasinor, one of India’s most unique geological attractions located near the historic town of Balasinor. Often referred to as India’s Jurassic Park, this fascinating site offers visitors a rare opportunity to witness real dinosaur fossil remains, including eggs, bones, and nesting grounds dating back over 65 million years. Situated in the Mahisagar district, the park provides guided tours led by knowledgeable experts who bring the ancient world to life with engaging stories and scientific insights. The on-site museum showcases well-preserved fossils, informative exhibits, and interactive displays, making it an ideal destination for families, students, and history enthusiasts. Easily accessible from Ahmedabad, this offbeat destination adds a distinctive touch to Gujarat tourism, combining education, adventure, and heritage in a truly unforgettable experience.
Jama Masjid
The magnificent Jama Masjid is one of the most remarkable historical landmarks in Ahmedabad and a must-visit attraction for travelers exploring Gujarat. Built in 1424 by Sultan Ahmed Shah, the founder of the city, this grand mosque beautifully reflects Indo-Islamic architecture blended with elements of Hindu and Jain craftsmanship. Constructed with warm yellow sandstone, the mosque features a vast courtyard that can accommodate thousands of devotees and visitors at once. The prayer hall is supported by more than 250 intricately carved pillars and crowned with 15 elegant domes that create a peaceful and majestic atmosphere. Delicate lattice screens, finely sculpted arches, and symmetrical design highlight the artistic brilliance of the medieval era. Located in the heart of the old city near Manek Chowk, Jama Masjid stands as a symbol of Ahmedabad?s rich cultural heritage and spiritual harmony. Tourists visiting the mosque can admire its stunning architecture, serene surroundings, and historic importance, making it one of the most iconic monuments and a key highlight of Gujarat tourism
Kankaria Lake
Kankaria Lake is one of Ahmedabad?s most vibrant and popular recreational attractions, offering a perfect blend of heritage, leisure, and family entertainment in the heart of the city. Originally built in the 15th century during the reign of Sultan Qutb-ud-Din, this historic circular lake has been beautifully redeveloped into a lively waterfront destination that attracts thousands of visitors every day. The well-maintained lakefront promenade features a variety of attractions including the famous toy train ride around the lake, the Kamla Nehru Zoological Garden, a kids? city, water rides, amusement parks, and the picturesque Nagina Wadi island garden located at the center of the lake. Visitors can also enjoy boating, tethered balloon rides for aerial views of Ahmedabad, cycling tracks, food courts, and evening musical fountain shows that create a festive atmosphere. Especially stunning after sunset when the entire lakefront lights up, Kankaria Lake offers a perfect outing for families, couples, and tourists looking to experience one of the most lively and entertaining public spaces.
Law Garden Night Market
The Law Garden Night Market is one of the most vibrant and culturally rich shopping destinations in Ahmedabad, offering visitors a lively glimpse into Gujarat?s traditional crafts, street culture, and local flavors. Located along the famous Law Garden area in the heart of the city, this bustling night bazaar comes alive after sunset and attracts tourists as well as locals looking for authentic Gujarati handicrafts and delicious street food. The market is especially popular for its colorful embroidered garments, traditional chaniya cholis, mirror-work textiles, handcrafted jewelry, bandhani fabrics, and decorative home items created by local artisans from across Gujarat. Visitors can stroll through dozens of brightly lit stalls, bargain with friendly vendors, and experience the energetic atmosphere filled with music, laughter, and aromas of local cuisine. Just opposite the market lies a famous food street where travelers can taste authentic Gujarati snacks such as pav bhaji, dabeli, kulfi, and fafda-jalebi. Law Garden Night Market perfectly blends shopping, culture.
Little Rann of Kutch
The Little Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is a mesmerizing salt desert known for its unique landscape, rich biodiversity, and cultural heritage, making it one of the most fascinating destinations for nature lovers and wildlife enthusiasts in western India. Spanning thousands of square kilometers, this vast white expanse transforms dramatically with the seasons, offering surreal views of salt flats, shimmering horizons, and golden sunsets. The region is home to the famous Indian Wild Ass, found primarily in the protected Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary, along with desert foxes, migratory birds, flamingos, pelicans, and numerous other species that thrive in this harsh yet beautiful ecosystem. Visitors can enjoy thrilling jeep safaris, birdwatching experiences, and cultural encounters with the traditional Agariya salt workers who have harvested salt here for generations. Located within easy reach of cities like Ahmedabad and Rajkot, the Little Rann of Kutch offers a perfect blend of wildlife adventure, desert landscapes, and authentic rural culture, making it an essential destination for travelers.
Manek Chowk
Manek Chowk in Ahmedabad is one of the most vibrant and historic marketplaces in Gujarat, famous for its unique transformation from a busy jewelry and textile trading hub during the day to a lively street food paradise at night. Located in the heart of the old city near iconic landmarks such as Bhadra Fort and Jama Masjid, this legendary square perfectly reflects the cultural charm and heritage of Ahmedabad. During the daytime, visitors can explore traditional gold and silver jewelry shops, local traders, and bustling bazaars that showcase the city?s rich mercantile history. As evening falls, Manek Chowk dramatically changes into a famous open-air food market filled with colorful stalls and irresistible aromas. Tourists and locals gather here to enjoy popular delicacies like butter pav bhaji, chocolate sandwiches, kulfi, ghughra, dosa, and many other street food favorites. The lively atmosphere, bright lights, and constant energy make it a paradise for food lovers and photographers alike. For travelers exploring Gujarat tourism, Manek Chowk offers an unforgettable experience.
Nalsarovar Bird Sanctuary
Nalsarovar Bird Sanctuary, located around 60 km from Ahmedabad in Gujarat, is one of India?s largest wetland bird sanctuaries and a must-visit destination for nature lovers, birdwatchers, and wildlife photographers. Spread across nearly 120 square kilometers, this beautiful shallow lake ecosystem attracts more than 250 species of migratory and resident birds every year. During the winter months from November to February, thousands of migratory birds arrive from Siberia, Central Asia, and Europe, turning the sanctuary into a vibrant natural paradise. Visitors can enjoy early morning boat rides across the calm waters while spotting flamingos, pelicans, cranes, herons, egrets, and a wide variety of ducks resting on small islands locally called ?bets.? The peaceful sunrise views, rich biodiversity, and serene landscape make Nalsarovar a perfect escape from city life. Easily accessible from Ahmedabad, the sanctuary is one of the most popular eco-tourism attractions in Gujarat and an ideal destination for day trips, birdwatching tours, nature photography.
Polo Forest
Located in the Sabarkantha district of Gujarat near the Rajasthan border, Polo Forest is one of the most beautiful eco-tourism destinations in the state and a perfect getaway for nature lovers, photographers, and heritage explorers. Nestled in the scenic foothills of the Aravalli Range along the peaceful Harnav River, the forest is famous for its lush greenery, rich biodiversity, historic ruins, and tranquil environment. The area is home to centuries-old temples and archaeological remains from the ancient Polo city that once thrived under the Parihar kings. Visitors can explore remarkable sites such as Sharneshwar Mahadev Temple, Surya Mandir, Polo Jain Temple, and the nearby Harnav and Vanaj dams, while enjoying activities like trekking, birdwatching, cycling, nature walks, and camping amidst bamboo groves and dense forest trails. The monsoon and post-monsoon seasons transform Polo Forest into a vibrant green paradise with flowing streams and misty hills, making it an ideal destination for eco tourism, weekend trips, and cultural exploration.
Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad
Located on the serene banks of the Sabarmati River in Ahmedabad, Sabarmati Ashram is one of Gujarat?s most important historical and cultural landmarks. Established in 1917 by Mahatma Gandhi, the ashram served as his residence and the center of India?s freedom movement for many years. It was from here that Gandhi launched the historic Dandi March in 1930, marking a significant moment in the struggle for independence. Today, the ashram stands as a peaceful memorial dedicated to Gandhian philosophy of truth, non-violence, and simple living. The complex includes Hriday Kunj, Gandhi?s modest home, along with a well-curated museum displaying rare photographs, personal letters, manuscripts, and the famous spinning wheel or charkha. Visitors can explore the tranquil gardens, galleries, and prayer grounds that reflect the inspiring life and teachings of Mahatma Gandhi. Easily accessible from the Ahmedabad city center and the Sabarmati Riverfront, Sabarmati Ashram attracts history enthusiasts, students, and international tourists, making it a must-visit heritage attraction in Gujarat.
Santram Mandir Nadiad
The sacred Santram Mandir Nadiad is one of the most revered spiritual landmarks in Gujarat and a prominent pilgrimage destination in the heart of Nadiad city. Dedicated to the great saint Santram Maharaj, the temple attracts thousands of devotees and travelers throughout the year who visit to seek blessings and experience divine peace. The temple complex is known for its serene atmosphere, well-maintained premises, and traditional architecture that reflects the spiritual heritage of Gujarat. Devotees gather daily for darshan, prayers, and spiritual gatherings, creating a deeply devotional environment. Santram Mandir is also widely respected for its charitable activities including community meals, social service initiatives, and support for people in need, continuing the noble teachings of Santram Maharaj. Important festivals such as Ram Navami, Guru Purnima, and Diwali are celebrated here with great enthusiasm and attract large numbers of pilgrims from across the state.
Science City, Ahmedabad
Gujarat Science City, Ahmedabad is one of the most exciting and educational tourist attractions in Gujarat, designed to make science engaging, interactive, and enjoyable for visitors of all ages. Spread across a vast campus on the Sarkhej?Gandhinagar Highway, Science City offers a perfect blend of education, innovation, and entertainment, making it a must-visit destination for families, students, and curious travelers. The complex features world-class attractions such as the Aquatic Gallery with its spectacular underwater tunnel, the Hall of Space that showcases fascinating facts about the universe, the Robotics Gallery highlighting modern technological advancements, and the impressive IMAX 3D Theatre that provides an immersive cinematic experience. Visitors can also explore the Energy Park, Planet Earth Pavilion, and beautifully designed science exhibits that demonstrate scientific concepts through fun and interactive displays. The evening musical fountain and light shows add further charm to the visit, creating a vibrant atmosphere for tourists.
Sidi Saiyyed Mosque
The Sidi Saiyyed Mosque is one of the most iconic historical landmarks of Ahmedabad and a remarkable example of Indo-Islamic architecture in Gujarat. Built in 1573 during the final years of the Gujarat Sultanate, the mosque is world famous for its exquisitely carved stone lattice windows, known as jalis, which beautifully showcase the artistic brilliance of that era. The most celebrated feature is the legendary ?Tree of Life? jali, a delicate stone carving depicting intertwined branches and leaves, now considered a timeless symbol of Ahmedabad?s rich heritage. Located in the heart of the city near Lal Darwaja, this architectural gem attracts history enthusiasts, photographers, and travelers from around the world who come to admire its intricate craftsmanship and serene atmosphere. Though modest in size, the mosque holds immense cultural significance and reflects the refined artistry of Gujarat?s medieval architecture. The peaceful surroundings, elegant arches, and stunning stone filigree make Sidi Saiyyed Mosque a must-visit heritage attraction for anyone exploring Ahmedabad.
Swaminarayan Akshardham
Swaminarayan Akshardham near Ahmedabad in Gandhinagar is one of Gujarat?s most magnificent spiritual and cultural landmarks, attracting devotees and tourists from across India and the world. Built in pink sandstone, this grand temple complex is dedicated to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and showcases intricate carvings, beautifully landscaped gardens, and inspiring exhibitions that narrate Indian culture, spirituality, and timeless values. Visitors can explore the main mandir, serene Sahajanand Van, engaging cultural galleries, and evening light and sound shows that bring history and devotion alive. Located about 25 km from central Ahmedabad, Akshardham offers a peaceful and enriching experience, making it a must-visit attraction for pilgrims, families, and travelers exploring Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar alike. The monument also features informative displays on the life and teachings of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, making it both a sacred pilgrimage site and an educational destination. With excellent facilities, security, and well-maintained surroundings, the complex stands as a symbol of devotion.

Ahmedabad – Heritage City of Gujarat
Ahmedabad is a remarkable heritage destination where centuries of history, traditional architecture, vibrant culture, and modern urban life come together. Founded by Sultan Ahmed Shah in 1411 on the eastern bank of the Sabarmati River, the city's historic walled area has preserved a distinctive architectural and cultural identity for centuries. The Historic City of Ahmedabad was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017, making it India's first World Heritage City.
The heart of Ahmedabad's heritage lies within its historic walled city, where magnificent monuments from the Sultanate period stand alongside Hindu and Jain temples, mosques, tombs, traditional residences, and bustling markets. The city is particularly renowned for its traditional pols—closely connected residential neighbourhoods featuring beautifully carved wooden houses, courtyards, community spaces, bird feeders, wells, and places of worship.

Experience the timeless charm of Ahmedabad at House of MG, a beautifully restored heritage hotel located in the heart of the city's historic old quarter. Housed in the former residence of the prominent Mangaldas Girdhardas family, this elegant property brings together Ahmedabad's rich architectural heritage, traditional craftsmanship, Gujarati hospitality, and modern comfort.

Day 01 : Arrival at Rajkot – Drive to Dwarka (Approx. 225 km / 5 hrs)
Upon your arrival at Rajkot Airport or Railway Station, you will be greeted by our tour representative. From here, begin your spiritual journey with a scenic drive to the holy town of Dwarka, one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites and among the oldest cities in India associated with Lord Krishna. En route, enjoy views of Gujarat’s countryside and rural charm. On arrival, check-in at the hotel and relax. In the evening, visit the Dwarkadhish Temple, dedicated to Lord Krishna. Witness the majestic evening aarti and explore the Gomti Ghat, located behind the temple. Overnight stay in Dwarka.
Day 02 : Dwarka – Bet Dwarka – Nageshwar – Dwarka (Approx. 80 km round trip)
After breakfast, proceed for a full-day excursion covering key spiritual landmarks around Dwarka. Begin with a visit to Bet Dwarka, located about 30 km away. A short ferry ride from Okha Port takes you to this sacred island believed to be the original residence of Lord Krishna. Visit the Bet Dwarkadhish Temple and enjoy the sea views.
On your way back, stop at the Nageshwar Jyotirlinga Temple, one of the 12 sacred Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. Also visit the serene Gopi Talav, associated with the divine tales of Krishna and the Gopis. Later, return to Dwarka and if time permits, explore Rukmini Devi Temple, dedicated to Krishna’s consort. Overnight stay in Dwarka.
Day 03 : Dwarka – Porbandar – Somnath (Approx. 230 km / 5.5 hrs)
Today after breakfast, depart for Somnath, with a stop at Porbandar (approx. 110 km from Dwarka). Porbandar is the birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi, and you’ll visit Kirti Mandir, a memorial built at his ancestral home. Also visit Sudama Temple, dedicated to Lord Krishna’s childhood friend.
Continue your drive to Somnath (approx. 120 km), one of the most important pilgrimage destinations in India. On arrival, check-in at the hotel. Later, visit the magnificent Somnath Temple, a Jyotirlinga shrine known for its spiritual significance and stunning seaside location. Don’t miss the Sound & Light Show in the evening that narrates the temple’s history. Overnight stay in Somnath.
Day 04 : Somnath – Diu – Somnath (Approx. 180 km round trip / 4 hrs total driving)
After breakfast, proceed for a day excursion to Diu, the former Portuguese colony and now a laid-back beach destination. Visit the impressive Diu Fort, St. Paul’s Church, and the mystical Naida Caves. Spend time at Nagoa Beach or enjoy local seafood at a beach shack.
In the late afternoon, return to Somnath. Optional: Revisit the temple for evening Dharshan or spend time near the Triveni Sangam, where three rivers meet the Arabian Sea. Overnight stay in Somnath.
Day 05 : Somnath – Sasan Gir (Approx. 70 km / 2 hrs)
This morning, after breakfast, drive to Sasan Gir, the only natural habitat of the Asiatic Lions in the world. Upon arrival, check in to your jungle resort and relax. In the afternoon, set out on an exciting jeep safari (subject to availability and permits) in Gir National Park, home not only to lions but also leopards, antelopes, jackals, and a rich variety of birds. Enjoy the wilderness and return to the resort. Overnight stay in Sasan Gir.
Day 06 : Sasan Gir – Junagadh (Approx. 60 km / 1.5 hrs)
After breakfast, proceed to Junagadh, an ancient princely state rich in historical and cultural heritage. Visit the magnificent Uparkot Fort, famous for its massive walls, Buddhist caves, and stepwells. Explore the ornate Mahabat Maqbara, a blend of Indo-Islamic architecture, and visit Ashokan Rock Edicts, bearing inscriptions from the Mauryan emperor.
If time permits, visit the base of Mount Girnar, a sacred hill dotted with Jain and Hindu temples. Overnight stay in Junagadh.
Day 07 : Junagadh – Rajkot (Approx. 105 km / 2.5 hrs)
After breakfast, begin your journey back to Rajkot, a vibrant city with a mix of colonial history and modern Gujarat charm. On arrival, check in to the hotel. Time permitting, visit Kaba Gandhi no Delo (Gandhi’s childhood home), Watson Museum, or stroll through Race Course Road for local shopping and food. Overnight stay in Rajkot.
Day 08 : Departure from Rajkot
After breakfast, check out from the hotel and transfer to Rajkot Airport or Railway Station for your onward journey with a heart full of divine blessings and cherished memories from Gujarat’s temples, forts, forests, and beaches.

Day 01 : Arrival in Ahmedabad – Welcome to Gujarat
Upon arrival at Ahmedabad Airport or Railway Station, you’ll be welcomed by our tour representative. Ahmedabad, the state’s cultural capital, is a blend of old-world charm and modern vibrance. Transfer to the hotel and check in. Later, explore some of the city’s highlights like the iconic Sidi Saiyyed Mosque, the peaceful Sabarmati Ashram, and enjoy an evening walk along the Sabarmati Riverfront. If time permits, visit Manek Chowk for a taste of local street food. Overnight stay in Ahmedabad.
Day 02 : Ahmedabad – Patan – Little Rann of Kutch (Approx. 280 km / 6 hrs)
After breakfast, proceed to Patan (approx. 125 km), a city steeped in history. Visit the UNESCO World Heritage site Rani ki Vav, a 11th-century stepwell known for its stunning sculptures. Continue to Modhera (35 km), home to the magnificent Sun Temple built by the Solanki dynasty, designed in perfect alignment with the solar equinox.
Later, drive towards Little Rann of Kutch (approx. 120 km), known for its unique salt marshes and wildlife. Upon arrival, check-in at a resort near Dasada. In the evening, you may opt for a short jeep safari to spot wildlife such as the Indian Wild Ass, desert foxes, and a variety of migratory birds. Overnight stay at Little Rann.
Day 03 : Little Rann of Kutch – Bhuj (Approx. 260 km / 5.5 hrs)
Early morning jeep safari (optional) in the Wild Ass Sanctuary, one of India's last refuges for this rare species. After breakfast, check out and proceed to Bhuj, the gateway to Kutch. En route, enjoy the changing landscapes as you enter the culturally rich Kutch region. Upon arrival, check in to the hotel.
Later, visit the Aina Mahal (Palace of Mirrors), Prag Mahal, and the Bhuj Museum to get insights into Kutch's royal and cultural heritage. Evening free for leisure or local market exploration. Overnight stay in Bhuj.
Day 04 : Bhuj Local Sightseeing & Bhujodi Village
Post breakfast, visit Bhujodi, a craftsman’s village just 8 km away, famous for its weaving, embroidery, and handicrafts. You can witness artisans at work and shop directly from local weavers. Return to Bhuj and visit Shree Swaminarayan Temple, known for its intricate white marble carvings.
In the evening, visit the Kutch Craft Museum and explore the colourful local markets for Bandhani fabrics and Kutchi jewellery. Overnight stay in Bhuj.
Day 05 : Bhuj – Mandvi (Approx. 60 km / 1.5 hrs)
After a leisurely breakfast, drive to Mandvi, a charming coastal town. On arrival, check in to the resort or beach camp. Visit the Vijay Vilas Palace, a royal summer retreat set amidst manicured gardens and a private beach. Later, relax at Mandvi Beach, known for its clean sands and calm waters.
In the evening, explore the local shipbuilding yard where wooden ships are still handcrafted using traditional techniques. Overnight stay in Mandvi.
Day 06 : Mandvi – Jamnagar (Approx. 300 km / 6.5 hrs)
Check out early and begin your drive to Jamnagar, known for its temples, lakes, and brass industries. On arrival, visit the Lakhota Lake and Palace, a peaceful spot with great birdlife. Also visit Bala Hanuman Temple, which holds a Guinness record for continuous chanting of the “Ram Dhun” since 1964.Evening at leisure. Overnight stay in Jamnagar.
Day 07 : Jamnagar – Dwarka (Approx. 130 km / 3 hrs)
Post breakfast, drive to the sacred city of Dwarka, one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites. On arrival, check in and later visit the legendary Dwarkadhish Temple, dedicated to Lord Krishna. Explore the Rukmini Devi Temple, Sudama Setu, and take a dip (optional) at the Gomti Ghat.In the evening, attend the Aarti at Dwarkadhish Temple. Overnight stay in Dwarka.
Day 08 : Dwarka – Porbandar – Somnath (Approx. 240 km / 5.5 hrs)
After breakfast, depart for Somnath. En route, stop at Porbandar (approx. 105 km), the birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi. Visit Kirti Mandir and the ancient Sudama Temple.
Continue to Somnath (approx. 135 km). Upon arrival, visit the majestic Somnath Temple, one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. Also visit Triveni Sangam, Bhalka Tirth, and Light & Sound Show (subject to availability). Overnight stay in Somnath.
Day 09 : Somnath – Diu (Approx. 90 km / 2 hrs)
After breakfast, drive to Diu, a serene coastal town that once served as a Portuguese colony. Check in upon arrival and begin sightseeing with Diu Fort, offering panoramic views of the Arabian Sea. Visit St. Paul’s Church, Naida Caves, and Gangeshwar Mahadev Temple.
Relax at Nagoa Beach or enjoy optional water sports. Overnight stay in Diu.
Day 10 : Diu – Sasan Gir (Approx. 100 km / 2.5 hrs)
After breakfast, proceed to Sasan Gir, home to the majestic Asiatic Lions. Upon arrival, check in to the jungle resort. In the afternoon, enjoy a jeep safari (subject to permit availability) in Gir National Park, the only place in Asia where lions roam freely in the wild.
Spend the evening in the natural surroundings or enjoy cultural activities organised by the resort. Overnight stay in Sasan Gir.
Day 11 : Sasan Gir – Junagadh (Approx. 60 km / 1.5 hrs)
Post breakfast, check out and drive to Junagadh, a city steeped in history and mythology. Visit Uparkot Fort, Mahabat Maqbara, and Ashokan Rock Edict — bearing inscriptions from the 3rd century BCE.
If time permits, visit Mount Girnar base (or take the ropeway if open) to get a glimpse of the sacred hill. Overnight stay in Junagadh.
Day 12 : Junagadh – Palitana – Bhavnagar (Approx. 215 km / 5 hrs)
After an early breakfast, drive to Palitana, one of Jainism's holiest pilgrimage sites. Climb (or take the doli/palki) up Shatrunjaya Hill to explore the cluster of 900+ intricately carved Jain temples.
After the spiritual experience, continue your journey to Bhavnagar (approx. 55 km). Check in and relax. Overnight stay in Bhavnagar.
Day 13 : Bhavnagar – Velavadar – Ahmedabad Drop (Approx. 220 km / 5.5 hrs)
After breakfast, check out and drive to Velavadar Blackbuck National Park (Approx. 50 km), famous for its large population of Blackbucks, wolves, and birdlife. Spend time in nature before heading to Lothal (approx. 90 km), one of the most prominent cities of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization. Visit the archaeological site and museum.
By evening, reach Ahmedabad (approx. 80 km from Lothal) and drop at the airport or railway station for your onward journey.

Day 01 : Ahmedabad – Sasan Gir (Approx. 375 km / 7.5 hours)
Upon your arrival in Ahmedabad, you will be warmly received by our representative. Begin your scenic road journey to Sasan Gir, located in the Junagadh district of Gujarat, which is home to the last remaining Asiatic lions in the wild. The drive, covering approximately 375 kilometers, takes around 7.5 hours and takes you through Gujarat’s semi-arid landscapes, dotted with farmlands and traditional villages. Upon arrival in Gir, check in to your forest resort or lodge and relax after the long journey. The rest of the evening is at your leisure—enjoy the natural surroundings or take a nature walk within the property. Overnight stay in Sasan Gir.
Day 02 : Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary
Start your day with an early morning breakfast at the hotel and prepare for an adventurous wildlife experience. Head to the Gir National Park for a guided jungle safari (advance booking recommended), where you’ll have the rare opportunity to spot the majestic Asiatic lions, as well as leopards, hyenas, jackals, crocodiles, and a rich diversity of birds and herbivores such as chinkara, nilgai, and sambar deer. After the safari, return to the hotel for lunch and some rest. In the afternoon, you may choose to visit the Gir Interpretation Zone at Devaliya, a fenced area designed for safe and easy wildlife viewing, especially if lion sightings were missed during the open safari. Optional evening activities include a visit to a nearby Maldhari tribal village to learn about the traditional pastoral lifestyle. Overnight stay in Sasan Gir.
Day 03 : Sasan Gir – Ahmedabad (Approx. 375 km / 7.5 hours)
After enjoying your morning breakfast at the hotel, check out and begin your return journey to Ahmedabad, covering the same route back through Gujarat’s rural heartland. The drive of approximately 375 kilometers will take around 7.5 hours, with en route stops for refreshments and local shopping if time permits. Upon arrival in Ahmedabad, you will be dropped at your preferred location—airport, railway station, or hotel—marking the end of your thrilling wildlife getaway in Sasan Gir.

Day 01 : Bhuj – Dhordo (White Rann of Kutch)
On arrival at Bhuj Railway Station or Bhuj Airport, guests are warmly received and transferred to the Rann Utsav Tent City at Dhordo, located on the edge of the world-famous White Rann of Kutch (approx. 85 km / 1.5–2 hours drive). En route, experience the changing landscape of Kutch’s vast plains. Upon arrival at the tent city, guests check in and are welcomed with refreshments. After enjoying a sumptuous lunch, the afternoon is free to explore the beautifully designed tent city, local handicraft stalls, art installations, and activity zones showcasing the vibrant culture of Kutch. In the evening, guests proceed to the White Rann, a spectacular salt desert, to witness a mesmerizing sunset, when the white salt turns golden and pink under the setting sun. The day concludes with a delicious dinner followed by captivating folk dance and cultural performances, offering an authentic taste of Kutchi traditions. Overnight stay at the Rann Utsav Tent City.
Day 02 : Rann Utsav Experience – Kala Dungar – Gandhi Nu Gaam
The day begins early with tea, followed by an optional visit to the White Rann for sunrise, a serene and unforgettable experience as the sun rises over the endless salt desert. After returning to the tent city, guests enjoy a hearty breakfast. The rest of the morning is at leisure to participate in various in-house activities such as camel rides, ATV rides, paramotoring (optional and chargeable), yoga sessions, shopping for local handicrafts, or simply relaxing and soaking in the festive atmosphere. After lunch, guests proceed for an excursion to Kala Dungar (Black Hill), the highest point in Kutch, offering panoramic views of the Great Rann and the Indo-Pakistan border region. The tour also includes a visit to Gandhi Nu Gaam, a reconstructed village showcasing traditional Kutchi houses, crafts, and rural lifestyle. In the evening, guests return to the tent city for dinner and enjoy another night of lively cultural programs and entertainment. Overnight stay at the tent city.
Day 03 : Dhordo – Bhuj Departure
After early morning tea and breakfast, guests check out from the tent city. The journey continues towards Bhuj with an en-route visit to Smritivan – The Earthquake Memorial Museum (subject to operational days), a world-class museum dedicated to the resilience of Kutch, offering panoramic views of Bhuj city from Bhujiyo Dungar. After the visit, guests are transferred to Bhuj Railway Station or Bhuj Airport for their onward journey, carrying unforgettable memories of the White Rann, vibrant culture, and unique desert festival experience.

The drive offers a refreshing change in landscape as you climb into Gujarat’s only designated hill station, nestled amidst lush greenery. Later, head to Sunset Point or Table Point for panoramic views and fun activities like horse riding and camel rides.

Day 01 : Arrival at Rajkot – Drive to Junagadh (Approx. 105 km / 1.5 to 2 hours)
Upon arrival at Rajkot Airport or Railway Station, you will be welcomed by our tour representative and driven to the historic city of Junagadh, nestled at the foot of the Girnar Hills. After check-in at your hotel, begin exploring Junagadh’s fascinating blend of Hindu, Jain, Buddhist, and Islamic heritage. Visit the majestic Uparkot Fort, with its deep moats, ancient stepwells like Adi Kadi Vav, and panoramic views. Continue to the beautiful Mahabat Maqbara, an architectural marvel combining Indo-Islamic and Gothic styles. If time permits, visit the ancient Ashokan Rock Edicts, dating back to the 3rd century BCE. Overnight stay in Junagadh.
Day 02 :  Junagadh – Sasan Gir (Approx. 65 km / 1 to 1.5 hours)
After breakfast, head to Sasan Gir, home to the world-famous Gir National Park, the last abode of the Asiatic Lion. On arrival, check in at your jungle resort or lodge. In the afternoon, embark on an exhilarating jeep safari through the Gir forest (subject to permit availability). During the safari, you might spot Asiatic lions, leopards, deer, crocodiles, and over 300 species of birds. After an adventurous day, unwind amidst nature and enjoy a traditional meal at the lodge. Overnight stay in Sasan Gir.
Day 03 : Sasan Gir – Somnath (Approx. 50 km / 1 to 1.5 hours)
Begin your day with an early morning safari (optional), or enjoy a peaceful nature walk around your stay. Post breakfast, proceed to the revered town of Somnath, one of the Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva and a sacred pilgrimage site on the Arabian Sea coast. On arrival, visit the magnificent Somnath Temple, rebuilt several times over the centuries and now a symbol of eternal spirituality. Witness the Sound and Light Show in the evening that narrates the temple’s storied history. Also visit Bhalka Tirth, where Lord Krishna is believed to have left his earthly body, and Triveni Sangam, the confluence of three holy rivers. Overnight stay in Somnath.
Day 04 : Somnath – Diu (Approx. 85 km / 2 hours)
After breakfast, depart for Diu, a charming coastal town that was once a Portuguese colony. Upon arrival, check in at your beachside hotel and begin exploring the highlights of this laid-back destination. Visit the mighty Diu Fort, offering splendid sea views, followed by the elegant St. Paul’s Church, a fine example of baroque architecture. Explore the unique Naida Caves, formed naturally and partially sculpted by human hands. Later, relax at Nagoa Beach or enjoy water sports (seasonal). In the evening, soak in the sunset at Chakratirth Beach. Overnight stay in Diu.
Day 05 :  Diu – Tulsi Shyam via Droneshwar Mahadev (Approx. 180 km / 4 to 5 hours)
After breakfast, set off for Tulsi Shyam, a revered spiritual and natural site located in the Gir Forest region. En route, make a meaningful stop at the Droneshwar Mahadev Tirth Dham, a peaceful temple complex known for its tranquil surroundings and religious significance. After paying homage, continue the scenic drive through the forested belt to Tulsi Shyam, known for its ancient hot sulfur springs, the Tulsi Shyam Temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu, and its serene jungle setting. In the evening, enjoy a nature walk and experience the spiritual calm of the forest. Overnight stay at Tulsi Shyam guest house or forest lodge.
Day 06 : Tulsi Shyam – Rajkot (Approx. 170 km / 4 to 5 hours)
After a leisurely breakfast, drive back to Rajkot, passing through small towns and the rustic landscapes of Gujarat. On arrival, check in at your hotel. If time permits, you can explore some local attractions such as the Watson Museum, Kaba Gandhi No Delo (the childhood home of Mahatma Gandhi), or shop for traditional Bandhani textiles and local snacks. Enjoy your last evening in the cultural heart of Saurashtra. Overnight stay in Rajkot.
Day 07 : Departure from Rajkot
After breakfast, you will be transferred to Rajkot Airport or Railway Station for your onward journey. This concludes your spiritual and natural journey through Gujarat’s rich tapestry of heritage, wildlife, temples, and coastlines, leaving you with cherished memories.

Day 01 :  Arrival in Leh
Welcome to Leh – the capital of Ladakh and one of the highest inhabited towns in the world. Upon arrival at Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport (3,500 m), our local representative will assist with your transfer to the hotel. Today is reserved for rest and altitude acclimatization due to the region’s thin air. You can opt for a light walk later in the day to visit nearby spots such as Leh Market, Shanti Stupa for a panoramic sunset, and the historic Leh Palace, offering majestic views of the Stok Kangri range.Overnight Stay at Leh.
Day 02 : Leh – Sham Region – Leh (124 Kms / 4–5 Hrs Round Trip)
After a refreshing breakfast at the hotel, proceed on an excursion to the Sham Valley region, also known as the “Apricot Valley.” Visit some of Ladakh’s iconic attractions: the mysterious Magnetic Hill, the sacred Gurudwara Pathar Sahib, and the breathtaking Sangam (confluence of the Indus and Zanskar Rivers). Continue to the beautiful and ancient Alchi Monastery, renowned for its 11th-century murals and Indo-Tibetan architecture. After exploring the region, return to Leh by evening.Overnight Stay at Leh.
Day 03 : Leh – Pangong Lake – Leh (280 Kms / 10–11 Hrs Round Trip)
Post an early breakfast at the hotel, set out for a full-day excursion to the magical Pangong Lake, located at an altitude of 4,350 meters. The journey takes you over the dramatic Changla Pass (5,360 meters), the third-highest motorable road in the world. Upon reaching Pangong, take in the surreal beauty of this endorheic lake, which stretches into China and changes shades from turquoise to deep blue. Capture the iconic 3 Idiots shooting point and soak in the tranquil vibes. Return to Leh in the evening.Overnight Stay at Leh.
Day 04 : Leh – Khardung La – Leh (78 Kms / 3–4 Hrs Round Trip)
After breakfast at the hotel, take a thrilling drive to the legendary Khardung La Pass (5,602 meters) — one of the world’s highest motorable roads. The route offers incredible views of snow-covered peaks, winding roads, and valleys stretching endlessly. You’ll have time to click photos at the summit and enjoy a cup of tea at the Khardung La café. Later, drive back to Leh, with optional stops at the Hall of Fame Museum and Spituk Monastery en route.Overnight Stay at Leh.
Day 05 : Leh – Tsomoriri Lake (240 Kms / 7–8 Hrs)
Post an early breakfast at the hotel, begin your journey towards the lesser-explored yet breathtaking Tsomoriri Lake, located in the Changthang Plateau at an altitude of 4,522 meters. The drive passes through the scenic Mahe Bridge and remote Himalayan villages. Upon arrival, witness the tranquil beauty of Tsomoriri Lake, surrounded by barren mountains and home to migratory birds, wild asses (kiangs), and marmots. The atmosphere is serene and untouched, ideal for photography and quiet reflection.Overnight Stay at Tsomoriri.
Day 06 : Tsomoriri – Tsokar – Taglang La – Leh (260 Kms / 8–9 Hrs)
After breakfast at the camp, depart for Leh via one of Ladakh’s most scenic and offbeat routes. En route, visit Tsokar Lake, a saltwater lake known for its stark white shores and avian diversity. The journey continues across the spectacular Taglang La Pass (5,328 meters), the second-highest motorable pass in Ladakh. Enjoy panoramic mountain vistas and unique high-altitude landscapes before descending into the Indus Valley and reaching Leh by evening.Overnight Stay at Leh.
Day 07 : Departure from Leh
After a memorable journey through Ladakh, enjoy your final breakfast at the hotel. Later, check out and transfer to Leh Airport for your onward flight. Take with you unforgettable memories of crystal-clear lakes, high mountain passes, ancient monasteries, and Ladakhi hospitality.

Day 01 :  Arrival at Jaipur – Bharatpur
UUpon your arrival at Jaipur Airport or Railway Station, you will be warmly received and then transferred to Bharatpur (185 km / approx. 4 hrs). Known for the famous Keoladeo Ghana National Park, Bharatpur is a paradise for bird watchers and nature lovers. On arrival, check into your hotel and relax for the day. Overnight stay in Bharatpur.
Day 02 : Bharatpur Sightseeing
After breakfast, proceed to explore the Keoladeo Ghana National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that attracts thousands of migratory birds each year, including Siberian cranes, pelicans, and herons. You can explore the park by cycle rickshaw or on foot for an up-close experience. Later, visit the Lohagarh Fort, known for its strength and history. Overnight stay in Bharatpur.
Day 03 :  Bharatpur – Ranthambore
After breakfast, check out and drive to Ranthambore (225 km / approx. 5 hrs), one of India's most celebrated wildlife destinations. On arrival, check in at your resort or hotel. The rest of the day is free at leisure. You may opt for an evening nature walk or enjoy the rustic village life surrounding the national park. Overnight stay in Ranthambore.
Day 04 :  Ranthambore Sightseeing (Safari Day)
Start your day early with a thrilling jeep safari inside Ranthambore National Park, home to the majestic Royal Bengal Tiger. After breakfast, visit the historic Ranthambore Fort, which offers panoramic views of the park and has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the afternoon, you can opt for another safari (optional, at extra cost) to increase your chances of spotting diverse wildlife. Overnight stay in Ranthambore.
Day 05 : Ranthambore – Bundi
After breakfast, check out and proceed to Bundi (130 km / approx. 3 hrs), a hidden gem of Rajasthan known for its forts, palaces, and stepwells. On arrival, check in and relax before heading out to explore Taragarh Fort, Sukh Mahal, and the beautifully carved Raniji Ki Baori (Queen’s Stepwell). Stroll through the quaint lanes of Bundi to experience its old-world charm. Overnight stay in Bundi.
Day 06 : Bundi – Pushkar
Post breakfast, begin your journey towards Pushkar (190 km / approx. 4.5 hrs), one of the oldest cities in India and a significant pilgrimage site. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel. Spend your evening exploring the Ghats of Pushkar Lake, and witness the mesmerizing aarti ceremony at sunset. Overnight stay in Pushkar.
Day 07 :   Pushkar Sightseeing
After breakfast, enjoy a full day of sightseeing in Pushkar. Visit the Brahma Temple, the only temple in India dedicated to Lord Brahma. Explore the colorful bazaars, and visit the Savitri Temple situated on a hilltop accessible via ropeway or trek, offering a panoramic view of the city. You may also take a camel ride through the desert areas. Overnight stay in Pushkar.
Day 08 : Pushkar – Jaipur
After breakfast, check out and drive to Jaipur (145 km / approx. 3 hrs), the vibrant capital of Rajasthan, known as the Pink City. On arrival, check in to your hotel and relax. In the evening, you may explore local markets such as Bapu Bazaar or enjoy a traditional Rajasthani dinner at a local restaurant or cultural venue. Overnight stay in Jaipur.
Day 09 : Jaipur Sightseeing
After breakfast, embark on a full-day sightseeing tour of Jaipur. Begin with the majestic Amber Fort, where you can ride an elephant or take a jeep to the top. Next, visit the City Palace, which houses museums and the royal residence. Continue to Jantar Mantar, the astronomical observatory, and stop for a photo at the iconic Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds). End your day at Jal Mahal (Water Palace) for a scenic photo opportunity. Overnight stay in Jaipur.
Day 10 : Departure
After breakfast, check out from your hotel and transfer to Jaipur Airport or Railway Station for your onward journey with cherished memories of your Rajasthan tour.

Welcome to Dubai, the city of dreams, futuristic architecture, and Arabian charm. Upon your arrival at Dubai International Airport (DXB), our representative will greet you and assist in your transfer to the hotel (approx. 15 km / 30 mins). After check-in, the rest of the day is at leisure. You may opt to explore the nearby Dubai Marina, stroll through The Walk at JBR, or visit Dubai Mall for a taste of the city’s upscale vibe. Overnight stay at your hotel in Dubai.
Day  2 : Dubai - Panoramic City Tour + Dhow Cruise with Dinner
After breakfast, embark on a half-day panoramic city tour of Dubai covering both historic and modern highlights (total drive approx. 40–50 km). Visit the stunning Jumeirah Mosque, enjoy a photo stop at the world-famous Burj Al Arab, and admire the architectural wonder of Palm Jumeirah and Atlantis The Palm. Explore Downtown Dubai, Sheikh Zayed Road, and the charming Al Bastakiya Quarter. End the tour with a visit to Dubai Creek and the colorful Gold & Spice Souks.
In the evening, enjoy a relaxing Dhow Cruise dinner along Dubai Creek or Marina (approx. 15 km to pier). Glide past illuminated cityscapes while savoring a buffet dinner onboard a traditional wooden dhow, with live music and entertainment. Return to the hotel for overnight stay.
Day  3 : Dubai - Thrilling Desert Safari on Sand Dunes
Morning at leisure. After lunch, set off on an unforgettable Desert Safari experience (approx. 50–60 km / 1 hr drive to Lahbab or Al Awir desert). Enjoy dune bashing in 4x4 SUVs driven by skilled professionals, then partake in camel rides, sandboarding, and henna painting at the desert camp.
As the sun sets, relax at a traditional Bedouin-style camp, where you’ll be treated to a BBQ dinner under the stars accompanied by belly dancing, Tanoura, and fire shows. Return to the hotel late evening. Overnight in Dubai.
Day  4 : Dubai – Burj Khalifa "At the Top" Experience
After a relaxed breakfast, head to the Burj Khalifa, the world’s tallest building (approx. 10 km from most city hotels). Ride the high-speed elevator to the 124th and 125th floors for the spectacular “At the Top” experience, offering panoramic views of the entire city, desert, and coastline.
Post-visit, spend time at the Dubai Mall, one of the world’s largest malls, where you can explore the Dubai Aquarium & Underwater Zoo, shop luxury brands, or enjoy a meal with a view of the Dubai Fountain show in the evening. Return to the hotel. Overnight in Dubai.
Day  5 : Dubai – Abu Dhabi + City Tour
After breakfast, proceed for a Abu Dhabi (approx. 140 km / 1.5 hours). On arrival check in to the hotel. Later Start with a visit to the magnificent Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, one of the largest mosques in the world and an architectural masterpiece.
Drive past the Emirates Palace, Corniche, and explore Heritage Village to understand the Emirati culture. Visit Qasr Al Watan (Presidential Palace, optional) or enjoy a photo stop at Etihad Towers. Later, return back to hotel. Overnight stay at the hotel.
Day  6 : Ferrari World Theme Park
After breakfast, proceed for a Ferrari World, the world’s first Ferrari-branded theme park. Enjoy thrilling rides like the Formula Rossa (world’s fastest rollercoaster), Flying Aces, and multiple family attractions, simulators, and interactive zones. Explore Italian dining outlets and Ferrari-inspired shopping.Later return back to the hotel for an overnight stay.
Day  7 : Departure
After breakfast and check-out, you will be transferred to  International Airport for your return flight. Depart with memories of Arabian adventures, architectural wonders, desert thrills, and luxury experiences.

Day 1 : Arrival At Zurich - Spiez
On Arrival, meet our representative outside and Your tour begins as with your Swiss Rail pass you take a train to Spiez.  A small town full of charm, Spiez is located in the heart of Switzerland on the banks of the deep-blue Lake Thun. In my opinion, this fairytale Swiss town is a real hidden gem in Switzerland.Surrounded by picturesque mountains, Spiez offers breathtaking views and a serene environment. It’s the perfect destination for anyone seeking a peaceful getaway from the hustle and bustle of city life.On arrival Check into the Hotel. Later take Lake Thun Cruise (Free with Swiss Rail Pass), here you can opt to visit St. Beatus Caves during the cruise.  Return back and Overnight in Spiez.
Day 2 : Spiez - Altesch Glacier - Spiez
After morning breakfast, today depart to see the longest glacier in the Alps - the Great Aletsch Glacier. Enjoy the breathtaking beauty of the panoramic views. Soak up the stunning scenery at this UNESCO World Heritage Site. Admire the full length and vastness of the Great Aletsch Glacier in all its glory from the viewing platform. Turn around and get a view of the higher peaks and most famous mountains of Switzerland. Observe the Mönch, the Eiger, the Jungfrau, the Wannenhorn, and the Finsteraarhorn. To the west of the area, admire the Weisshorn, the Mischabel group with the Dom, and the Matterhorn itself form a breathtaking 360° panorama. Return back and Overnight in Spiez
Day 3 : Spiez - Brienzer Rothorn - Spiez
Today after breakfast, Enjoy a nostalgic steam train experience on the rack-and-pinion railway. The steam locomotive and its red carriages will transport you through the verdant forests and on towards the summit. The longer the trip takes, the more breathtaking the views become. Rothorn Kulm summit station in just over an hour. The steam locomotive with its red carriages puffs its way up the mountain, passing through green forests and you will enjoy an incredible panorama of the surrounding mountains and turquoise-coloured Lake Brienz. The panoramic view from the summit is unforgettable.Later, Experience, Jetboat ride, 360° turns and excitement on the waters of Lake Brienzboat trip takes you from Bönigen to the imposing Giessbach Falls.. Marvel at the stunning mountain scenery and the breathtaking natural beauty during the tour. Overnight stay in this charming lakeside town of Spiez.
Day 4 : Spiez to Bern
Today after breakfast, depart to check in to the Million Stars Hotel, the most exciting hotel you’ll find in Switzerland! Here guests experience nature in its purest form – and in an entirely exclusive location meant for two. The kinds of accommodation on offer are as varied as their locations. But what they all have in common is an unobstructed view of the starry night sky. Overnight stay in Million star hotel.
Day 5 : Bern to Andermatt
Today after breakfast, check out and depart for Andermatt. Today you can opt to visit Oberalp Pass, which is a high mountain pass in the Swiss Alps connecting the cantons of Graubünden and Uri between Disentis/Mustér and Andermatt.?Visit the former front light from Hook of Holland, which was a 14-m-high lighthouse that shone out steadily for 70 years from the mouth of the Rhine at the other end of the river, now stands as a herald for the source of the Rhine on the Oberalp Pass. Overnight in Andermatt.
Day 6 : Andermatt - Lugano & Gandria - Andermatt
Today after breakfast, Escape the bustling city center with by a lake cruise from Lugano  through olive groves to the outlying village of Gandria. Stroll the Sentierodell'Olivo, taking in views of the almost Mediterranean landscape . Explore the streets of Gandria, then relax as a boat transports you across the lake, back to Lugano.Evening explore the Lugano Old town. Overnight in LuganoLater return back to the Hotel. Overnight in Andermatt.
Day 7 : Andermatt - Zurich
Today after breakfast, visit Uetliberg at 2,850 feet above sea level. The mountain offers an impressive panoramic view of the city, the lake and the Alps.In summer, there’s plenty to discover on well-marked hiking routes, a mountain bike route, and on the Planet Trail from Uetliberg to Felsenegg (Adliswil) takes you on a fascinating tour through a model of their solar system. In the winter, the hiking trails to the summit are converted into sledding runs here.Return back to Zurich, Explore the bahnofstrasse. Overnight in Zurich.
Day 8 : Departure
After breakfast, check out and depart to Zurich International Airport for your flight Back to Home.
